response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT s.healtheval AS healtheval, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON c.zoneref = s.zoneregistry GROUP BY s.healtheval), sh AS (SELECT healtheval, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT healtheval, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Conservation records are inner-joined to sites on zoneref = zoneregistry, so records with no matching site are dropped. The share's denominator is the total count of the remaining records.
A missing status means a NULL healtheval, which forms its own group. Empty strings, if any exist, would be a separate group.
The average share used for the above-average filter and for the excess is the simple average across all status groups, including the NULL group. It is not weighted by count.
